route.change: Think-SFT with the cue at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0 and the cap raised to 32,768, two samples per problem, keeping the shared answer if they agree, otherwise the sample that finished (not a cap hit), otherwise sample 0; rule computed afterwards from answers.jsonl.
route.gap_parts: Budget (cap hit): about a quarter of the gap (.25 on MATH-500 T 1.0, .27 on hard328), about 12 of the 46 hard328 problems between one cued-base sample (161) and one RL sample (207). The raised cap alone gave Think-SFT +23 on hard328 (207 to 230), and the finished-over-cut rule picks up a further ~5-8 where sample 0 is still cut at 32,768 and sample 1 finishes. Reliability (right in another draw): .43-.63 of the gap; a second draw only wins the cases where the two samples disagree and exactly one finished, so about 2-4 problems from it.
route.why: Ending is a sampled event and the cap cuts the long tail. Think-SFT's cut answers are unfinished work that comes out right at a high rate once it finishes, so a longer cap plus a second draw that prefers a finished sample turns cap hits into right answers more cheaply than a full vote over 4.
